outcome: MEASUREMENT (not a QPS win) — the reads-copy lever does not deliver a benchmark-provable end-to-end speedup; the single-copy change is a recall-identical code-quality byproduct
dataset: synthetic 200000×128 (distinct, seed 42) + SIFT 120000×128 (real, for the SBQ recall gate)

hardware.note: mobile CPU, thermal-throttled + heavy container load during measurement — HIGH variance; the measured effect is SMALLER than this variance

findings.claim: SBQ (scalar quantization, the original M38 approach) preserves recall to baseline
findings.evidence: theodb.sbq_knn vs exact seqscan on real SIFT 120k×128, 100 queries, f32 baseline recall@10 = 1.0000: SBQ bits=1/of=40 = 0.774; bits=2/of=40 = 0.854; bits=4/of=40 = 0.947 — all below 1.0. Scalar quantization loses too much ranking information per byte; PQ (product quantization + LUT asymmetric distance, the ScaNN/FAISS approach) is the technical answer but a large milestone.

findings.claim: the reads phase (~44% of the M36 profiler) is copy-dominated, so eliminating the copy speeds up the scan
findings.evidence: eliminated read_chunked's double-copy (read_page_item.to_vec() + extend_from_slice → read_page_item_into, one copy). The INTERNAL profiler reads dropped ~8ms→~4ms at probes=50, BUT the end-to-end QPS showed NO reliable win: ratio m38/m36 = {50:[1.03,1.52,0.94,1.03], 100:[1.16,0.94,0.94], 200:0.92} — swings 50% between runs = noise; effect < measurement variance. LESSON: the M36 profiler's phase attribution was INFLATED by its own Instant::now() instrumentation overhead (~400 syscalls/query at probes=50); the copy is not the real end-to-end bottleneck.

findings.claim: the double-copy in read_chunked is wasteful
findings.evidence: read_page_item_into appends directly (one copy) instead of read_chunked's old two copies + intermediate realloc. Recall byte-identical (61 coexistence tests return the same kNN ids). Merged as a code-quality refactor (less allocation/memory traffic), NOT as a QPS win — the benchmark does not support a performance claim (F2).

recall_preserved: IDENTICAL — the single-copy change copies the same bytes; kNN ids unchanged (61 coexistence tests: test_index_am/hnsw_structured/reloption/ann_index/sbq_index).

verdict.real_remaining_vector_lever: PQ (product quantization + ADC via LUT — the ScaNN algorithm); reduces candidates/bytes at preserved recall; PhD-level, a large future milestone
verdict.honest_note: measurement-first (3rd time in the M36/M38 saga) reshaped the milestone: SBQ regresses recall, and copy-elimination gives no end-to-end win because the profiler misled via instrumentation overhead. Shipping M38 as a QPS win would be unsupported by the data.

reproduction: SBQ recall: load SIFT subset into a table, theodb.sbq_knn vs seqscan. Copy QPS: PGPORT=<port> python3 benchmarks/run_m36_scan.py --n 200000 --probes 50 --k 10 --runs 10 (theo-db:m36 = double-copy, theo-db:m38 = single-copy).
